title: Carboplatin every three weeks for ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer
schedule_label: One infusion on day 1 every 21 days (three weeks). Bring your written next appointment date. Your team plans the number of cycles and reviews response, blood results and treatment tolerance.
schedule_summary: One infusion on day 1 every 21 days (three weeks). Bring your written next appointment date. Your team plans the number of cycles and reviews response, blood results and treatment tolerance.
purpose: After surgery, treatment may reduce the risk of the cancer returning. For advanced or recurrent disease, it aims to control cancer and symptoms. Ask which aim applies to you.
indication_text: Three groups are covered for epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal or fallopian tube cancer: after surgery when combination chemotherapy is unsuitable; first treatment of stage III–IV disease when surgery is infeasible and combination treatment unsuitable; or recurrence that remains sensitive to platinum.
administration_text: Carboplatin is given into a vein over about 30 minutes on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Blood checks and anti-sickness medicine add time to the visit. The team works out your dose from kidney function and a prescribed target exposure.
monitoring_summary: The team checks blood counts and kidney and liver function, reviews symptoms and signs of platinum allergy, and decides whether to give the next infusion.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Links strands of DNA together. Cancer cells then have difficulty dividing. The kidneys clear the medicine, so kidney function affects the prescribed dose.

common_effects.title: What you may notice
common_effects.text: Nausea, tiredness, altered taste and reduced appetite may follow treatment. Blood counts can fall between visits even when you feel well.

serious_effects.title: Infection or bleeding · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Ring urgently if you have a fever, chills, new bruising, nosebleeds or feel suddenly unwell.

serious_effects.title: Allergic reaction · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Tell the nurse right away about itching, flushing, throat tightness, wheeze or dizziness during treatment, even if earlier infusions went well.

serious_effects.title: Kidney function · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Report reduced urine and vomiting. Blood tests help your team calculate each dose.

serious_effects.title: Nausea and vomiting · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Take the anti-sickness treatment as written. Call if you cannot keep down fluids.

serious_effects.title: Nerve or hearing changes · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Report new tingling, numbness or ringing ears, particularly after previous platinum therapy.

questions.q: Why do I need another kidney test?
questions.a: The kidneys clear carboplatin. The team checks how well they are working to choose an appropriate dose for this cycle.

questions.q: How do I know when the next dose is due?
questions.a: Your booked schedule is every three weeks. A blood test or clinic visit is separate from an infusion. Use the date printed on your treatment plan.

questions.q: Which blood counts does my team look for?
questions.a: The usual minimum is 1 for neutrophils and 100 for platelets, both in billions per litre. A result exactly at either minimum meets that count threshold. Your team may choose a higher minimum for you and reviews the rest of your results and symptoms before giving treatment.

evidence.title: EWOC-1 and AGO-OVAR · treatment-setting evidence
evidence.interpretation: Studies compared carboplatin alone with combinations in people receiving their first treatment and in people whose cancer had returned. Some combinations controlled the cancer longer. Your team weighs this against which treatment you can tolerate.
evidence.limitations: The studies involve different settings and do not compare 21-day with 28-day administration. Neither provides an individual prognosis. EWOC-1 was stopped early in a selected vulnerable population; age alone does not establish that combination treatment is unsuitable.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests. A measured kidney filtration test is preferred where feasible because carboplatin dose depends on kidney clearance.
Mention previous platinum treatment or allergy, bleeding, infections and medicines that may affect the kidneys.

rows.label: Before each cycle
cells: The team checks blood counts and kidney and liver function, reviews symptoms and signs of platinum allergy, and decides whether to give the next infusion.
Call if fever or bleeding develops, even if a recent blood test was satisfactory.

rows.label: Response review
cells: Symptoms, examination and scans or tumour markers when appropriate help the team judge benefit.
Ask which measures will be used for your cancer and when you will discuss the results.

monitoring_schedule.note: The team individualises response assessments and extra tests according to symptoms and treatment aim.

prescription_phases.label: Day 1 · carboplatin every 21 days

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.timing: Up to three times daily · PRN / as directed
medicines.note: Leave at least 6 hours between doses. Maximum 5 days and 30 mg/day or 0.5 mg/kg/day, whichever is lower. Review extrapyramidal risk with olanzapine.

additional_support: Use the dated anti-sickness prescription for the scheduled platinum treatment. Ask which dose to take next and how to use rescue medicine.
prescription_notes: Use the carboplatin-specific high-risk antiemetic regimen. Check previous platinum reactions, tolerability, renal function and the dates of delayed anti-sickness medicine.
